Tesla Model Y Long Range

Trip Summary

A 22-day family road trip from Brossard, QC through five major American cities — Washington DC, Atlanta, Houston, Austin, and Dallas — returning via Nashville and Cleveland (direct home after Cleveland). Suburban hotels mean easy highway access; we're happy to drive into every city center for sightseeing.

⚡ Tesla EV Planning Notes

✓
Range: Tesla Model Y Long Range — ~430–460 km real-world highway range. Plan Supercharger stops every 350–400 km.
✓
Strategy: Charge to 80% between stops (faster charging), 100% only before long overnight segments or border crossings.
✓
Overnight: All cities have Tesla Superchargers — charge to 100% overnight at the hotel or nearby location before each driving day.
✓
Border crossing: Charge at Plattsburgh, NY before crossing back into Canada. Limited fast-charging immediately north of the border.
✓
August heat: AC use reduces range by ~10–15%. Budget slightly more stops than Tesla's navigation suggests on hot days.
✓
Pre-conditioning: Use the Tesla app to pre-cool the car before getting in during Texas summer (~38–40°C highs expected).

Family Travel Tips

🎒 Packing Essentials
  • Passports + US visa/ETA documents
  • Travel insurance (all 4 members)
  • CAA / roadside emergency kit
  • Tesla charging adapter (J1772)
  • Sunscreen & wide-brim hats (Texas heat)
  • Reusable water bottles (1 per person)
💰 Budget Planning
  • Book Space Center Houston in advance
  • Georgia Aquarium — buy tickets online (sells out)
  • US cash for border tolls and tips
  • Notify bank of travel dates before leaving
  • Many DC monuments and museums are FREE
  • Hermann Park and most TX parks are FREE
📅 Key Booking Reminders
  • Hotels for 5 city stops + 2 return overnights (Nashville & Cleveland)
  • Space Center Houston (timed entry)
  • Georgia Aquarium (popular, book early)
  • NASA tram tour (included, but limited capacity)
  • US Capitol tour (free, must book weeks ahead)
  • Teen ID or passport copy for border

Brossard, QC — Depart
Aim for 7:00 AM departure. Charge to 100% overnight. Cross US border at Champlain/Lacolle (A-15 S → I-87 S). Allow 20–40 min for border crossing.
Albany, NY  ⚡ Supercharger
~265 km from Brossard · arrive ~80% charge · charge to 80% (~20 min). Located off I-87. Good stretch break — grab coffee before continuing south.
Edison, NJ  ⚡ Supercharger
~500 km from Brossard · charge to 80% (~30 min). Good lunch stop. Route continues via I-78 W → I-95 S through New Jersey toward DC. Avoid peak NYC traffic if possible.
Washington DC — Arrive
~940 km from home · Estimated arrival 5:30–6:30 PM (incl. border). Check in to Embassy Suites and rest up for 4 days of sightseeing starting tomorrow.
Dining Top 5 Highly Rated Restaurants Near the Hotel (July 25 arrival dinner)

All within easy walking distance (5–10 minutes) from the Embassy Suites. Perfect for dinner after the long drive on July 25. Reservations recommended.

Zaytinya

4.7 ★ (20k+)
Mediterranean • José Andrés • 6 min walk

One of DC's most celebrated restaurants. Creative small plates inspired by Turkish, Greek & Lebanese cuisine. Perfect for sharing — hummus, grilled octopus, lamb, vegetarian options. Lively yet sophisticated. A must-try.

Centrolina

4.8 ★ (2.4k)
Italian • Penn Quarter • ~8 min walk

James Beard-recognized seasonal Italian by Chef Amy Brandwein. House-made fresh pasta, beautiful antipasti, and a market next door. Elegant but welcoming — excellent for all ages.

Yardbird Table & Bar

4.6 ★ (2.8k+)
Southern • Fried Chicken • ~7 min walk

Famous for outstanding fried chicken. Comforting Southern classics with a modern twist in a lively space. Great for teens and families.

Daikaya

4.3 ★ (3.8k+)
Japanese Ramen & Izakaya • Chinatown • ~8 min walk

Two experiences in one building: downstairs excellent Sapporo-style ramen (noodles from Japan), upstairs lively izakaya with small plates. Casual and fun — ramen is always a winner with teens.

Jaleo

4.7 ★ (high volume)
Spanish Tapas • José Andrés • ~8 min walk

Vibrant Spanish tapas — paella, gambas al ajillo, excellent sangria. Fun, energetic atmosphere that works great for families and groups. A DC classic.

Tip: Book ahead for arrival night. Ask the hotel front desk for same-day help or walk-in advice.

~1,020 km · Estimated arrival 6:00–7:00 PM. Check in to Hampton Inn Peachtree Corners. 5 great nights of Atlanta exploration start tomorrow.
Dining Top 5 Rated Restaurants Near the Hotel (July 29 arrival dinner)

All within ~2 km of Hampton Inn Peachtree Corners. Perfect for dinner after the long drive from DC. No need to venture far — great options right around the hotel.

Tortugas Cuban Grill

4.6 ★
Cuban & Latin • ~0.7 mi • $$–$$$

The highest rated restaurant in the area — a local gem with fresh, bold Cuban flavours. Must-orders: mofongo, ropa vieja, and the best tres leche cake in the area. Great mojitos and live music on weekends. Family-friendly with large portions.

J. Alexander's Restaurant

4.3 ★
American • ~1.5 mi • $$$

#1 ranked restaurant in the Peachtree Corners area. Upscale casual with generous portions. Known for prime rib, salmon, and handcrafted desserts. Popular with families — reservations recommended for dinner arrivals after 6 PM.

Stäge Kitchen & Bar

4.4 ★
American • ~1.0 mi • $$–$$$

Trendy neighbourhood bar and kitchen with a creative menu. Great cocktails and craft beers. Lively atmosphere — perfect for winding down after a long drive. Good mix of small plates and mains. Kid-friendly menu available.

'Cue Barbecue

4.3 ★
BBQ • ~0.8 mi • $$

Classic Southern BBQ — smoked brisket, pulled pork, and ribs. Walk-in friendly with no wait most evenings. Casual and relaxed, great for kids. One of the most consistent spots in the area for a filling, no-fuss first night meal.

Firebirds Wood Fired Grill

4.2 ★
Steakhouse • ~0.5 mi • $$$

Upscale wood-fired steakhouse within walking distance of the hotel. Excellent steaks, salmon, and wood-fired specialties. Great bar scene. Full family menu — a solid splurge option for the first night in Atlanta.

Tip: 'Cue Barbecue and Tortugas are walk-in friendly. J. Alexander's books up — call ahead if arriving after 6 PM.

Dining Top 5 Rated Restaurants Near the Hotel (August 3 arrival dinner)

All within ~1 km of Tru by Hilton Webster. Perfect for a late dinner after the longest driving day of the trip (Atlanta → Houston). Easy to reach straight from the hotel — no need to go further after ~14 hrs on the road.

Ohayo Sushi

4.4 ★
Sushi & Japanese • ~0.7 mi • $$

All-you-can-eat sushi for $20.95/person — made fresh to order, not a buffet. Famous for the NASA Roll. Large tables perfect for families. One of the best AYCE sushi spots in the Houston area. Kids love it. Open until 9:30 PM on weekdays.

Pappas Seafood House

4.5 ★
Seafood • ~0.3 mi • $$$

#2 restaurant in all of Webster on TripAdvisor. Family-owned since 1981 by a Greek fishing family. Generous portions of Gulf Coast seafood — shrimp, crab, fish platters. Busy but service is fast and efficient. A Texas seafood institution right on I-45 near NASA Rd.

Pappas Delta Blues Smokehouse

4.4 ★
BBQ & American • ~0.3 mi • $$–$$$

Southern BBQ done right — slow-smoked ribs, brisket, and pulled pork. Part of the well-loved Houston Pappas restaurant family. Great bar with cold drinks. Casual and welcoming, perfect for a tired family after a big drive. Walk-ins welcome.

Lupe Tortilla

4.3 ★
Tex-Mex • ~0.5 mi • $$–$$$

A Houston legend — homemade flour and corn tortillas, exceptional fajitas, and fresh salsa. Margaritas are famous. Colourful and lively atmosphere that kids enjoy. Consistent quality across visits. One of the most beloved Tex-Mex chains in the Houston area.

Pappasito's Cantina

4.1 ★
Mexican • ~0.4 mi • $$–$$$

Classic Houston Tex-Mex with sizzling fajitas and strong margaritas. Another Pappas family favourite — relaxed atmosphere, quick service, and kid-friendly menu. Great option if Lupe Tortilla has a long wait. Both are within the same 0.5 mi strip near the hotel.

Tip: Ohayo Sushi and Pappas Delta Blues are the most walk-in friendly. Pappas Seafood House can get busy — worth calling ahead if arriving after 8 PM. All are within a 5-minute drive of the hotel.

Washington DC

July 25 – 29, 2026  ·  4 nights

Many attractions are free

Embassy Suites by Hilton Washington DC Convention Center
900 10th Street NW, Washington, DC 20001
Check-in Jul 25 — Check-out Jul 29 (4 nights)
~10-20 min drive to the National Mall and downtown core (via I-395 or 14th St NW). Easy access — happy to drive in daily for sightseeing!
Day 1 Sunday, July 26, 2026 — Arrival & National Mall

Lincoln Memorial

FREE

Iconic marble memorial honoring President Abraham Lincoln. Features the famous Gettysburg Address engraving and offers beautiful views of the Reflecting Pool and Washington Monument. Great photo spot and powerful history lesson for teenagers.

Washington Monument

FREE

Tall obelisk honoring the first U.S. President, George Washington. Offers panoramic views of the National Mall from the top. Free timed tickets are recommended for the elevator ride — book online in advance.

Thomas Jefferson Memorial

FREE

Beautiful domed memorial on the Tidal Basin honoring Thomas Jefferson. Especially stunning in the evening or at night with the lights reflecting on the water. Easy to combine with Lincoln and Washington Monument for a classic National Mall evening.

Day 2 Monday, July 27, 2026 — Museums & Capitol

National Air and Space Museum

FREE

One of the most popular museums in the world. Home to the original Wright Flyer, Apollo 11 command module, and many historic aircraft and spacecraft. Extremely engaging for teenagers interested in science and history.

U.S. Capitol Visitor Center

FREE (timed)

Free guided tours of the U.S. Capitol building. Learn about American democracy and see the impressive architecture. Timed tickets must be booked in advance through the official website.

International Spy Museum

~$30/adult

One of the most popular and interactive museums in DC, especially great for teenagers. Real spy gadgets, interactive exhibits, and fascinating stories from the world of espionage. Located near the National Mall / L'Enfant Plaza. Highly recommended.

Day 3 Tuesday, July 28, 2026 — White House & Virginia Highlights

White House Visitor Center

FREE

Learn about the history and daily life inside the White House. View the building from outside (public tours are extremely limited). The Visitor Center offers excellent exhibits and videos.

George Washington Masonic National Memorial

~$18

Striking tower in Alexandria modeled after the ancient Lighthouse of Alexandria. Climb to the top for excellent views of DC and the Potomac. Interesting exhibits on George Washington and American history. ~15-20 min drive or easy Metro + short walk.

National Museum of the United States Army

FREE

Outstanding modern museum at Fort Belvoir (about 25-30 min drive south). Covers Army history from the Revolution through today with excellent interactive exhibits, vehicles, and personal stories. Highly recommended for history buffs and teens. Free parking on site.

~35-50 min drive to downtown Atlanta core via I-85. Suburban base with easy highway access — happy to drive in for sights, Georgia Aquarium, etc.!

Texas BBQ ahead — the master list

Next stop is Texas! Top 50 BBQ picks near your route are flagged on the Houston, Austin & Dallas tabs. Full source: Texas Monthly — Top 50 BBQ Joints, 2025 Edition.

Day 1 Thursday, July 30, 2026 — Attractions & Downtown

Georgia Aquarium

~$40/person

One of the largest aquariums in the world, home to whale sharks, beluga whales, manta rays, and thousands of marine species. Features immersive exhibits including a massive 10-million-gallon Ocean Voyager tank. A must-do for families — allow 3–4 hours. Book tickets online to skip lines.

World of Coca-Cola

~$20/person

A museum dedicated to the history and global culture of Coca-Cola, right next to the Georgia Aquarium. Highlights include a vault displaying the "secret formula," a 4D theater experience, and a tasting room with over 100 beverages from around the world. Teens love the tasting room.

Centennial Olympic Park

FREE

Built for the 1996 Atlanta Summer Olympics, this 22-acre downtown park is the perfect free outdoor stop between paid attractions. Features the iconic Fountain of Rings — the world's largest interactive Olympic rings fountain. Great for a break, photos, and a picnic. Adjacent to the aquarium and World of Coca-Cola.

Day 2 Friday, July 31, 2026 — Buford Highway & Chinese Community

Atlanta has one of the most vibrant Chinese and Pan-Asian communities in the American South, centred along Buford Highway NE in Chamblee and Doraville — about 20–30 min from the hotel. A full day of authentic food, culture, and exploration awaits.

Atlanta Chinatown Mall

Morning
Cultural Hub • Chamblee, GA • Free entry • Cash only inside

Atlanta's authentic Chinatown — tucked off I-285 and New Peachtree Road and serving the community since 1988. Food court with 6 restaurant stalls, a bakery, two dine-in restaurants, a full Chinese grocery store, a bookstore, art gallery, koi pond, and traditional gardens. Chinese, Taiwanese, Cantonese, Vietnamese, Laotian and Korean culture all in one compact space. The entrance lions and traditional architecture make a great photo stop. Bring cash — credit cards not accepted.

Buford Highway Farmers Market

Afternoon
International Market • Doraville, GA • Free entry • Open 8 AM–10 PM

A 100,000 sq ft indoor international food market — the best in the Southeast. Aisles from 71 countries: Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Latin American, Middle Eastern, Eastern European and more. Massive Asian produce section, specialty ingredients, grab-and-go sushi, dumplings, and a hot food bar. Budget 1.5–2 hours to explore. Kids love discovering unfamiliar snacks. Staff are happy to explain anything unfamiliar — a genuinely fun cultural adventure.

Best BBQ 來記燒臘

Lunch
Cantonese BBQ & Dim Sum • 5000 Buford Hwy NE, Doraville • $ • Counter service

Inside City Farmers Market — counter service Cantonese BBQ at its most authentic. Order the three-meat combo: roast pork belly (siu yuk), soy sauce chicken, and roast duck over rice. Dim sum options include siu mai and har gow. Unpretentious, fast, and genuinely delicious. A favourite of Atlanta's Chinese community — exactly the kind of place you won't find at home.

Northern China Eatery

Explore
Northern Chinese • 5141 Buford Hwy NE Ste C, Chamblee • $$ • Hidden gem

A beloved hidden gem — tucked beneath an eyeglass store on Buford Highway. Family-style Northern Chinese cooking: mix dumplings (three varieties), Mandarin Lion's Head meatballs, and Spicy Griddle Fish. Perfect for sharing around the table. A local favourite among Atlanta's Chinese diaspora. Try the hand-pulled noodles if available.

Gu's Kitchen

Snack / Explore
Sichuan Street Food • 4897 Buford Hwy Ste 104, Chamblee • $–$$

Authentic Sichuan street food done right. Mapo tofu, zhong-style dumplings in chili oil, and their playful "Sichuan French Fries." Balanced spice levels that work for adventurous eaters of all ages. Great for a mid-afternoon snack between the Chinatown Mall and Farmers Market. A must for anyone curious about real Sichuan flavours.

China Hot Pot

Dinner
Hot Pot • 5090 Buford Hwy NE, Doraville • $$ • AYCE $30/person

End the day with an interactive hot pot dinner — the perfect family meal. Choose your broth (mild, spicy, or split pot), then pick from an extensive menu of meats, seafood, vegetables, and noodles to cook at the table. All-you-can-eat at ~$30/person. Most items individually priced around $10. Kids love the interactive experience of cooking their own food. A fun, communal way to close out a day on Buford Highway.

Tip: Bring cash for Atlanta Chinatown Mall (cards not accepted). The whole Buford Highway corridor is within a few km — plan Chinatown Mall in the morning, Farmers Market in the early afternoon, lunch at Best BBQ or Northern China Eatery, and finish with hot pot dinner. ~25 min drive from Peachtree Corners hotel.

Day 3 Saturday, Aug 1, 2026 — Outdoors & Markets

Stone Mountain Park

~$20/car

A massive granite monadnock just 25 km east of downtown Atlanta, with a cable car to the summit, walking trails, and stunning panoramic views of the city. Great outdoor activity for the whole family. The park also features a skyride, mini-golf, and a popular laser show at dusk on summer evenings.

Ponce City Market & BeltLine

FREE entry

Ponce City Market is Atlanta's beloved food and retail hub inside a restored 1920s Sears building, with a rooftop carnival (paid) offering great city views. Connect directly to the Atlanta BeltLine — a 35 km urban trail loop lined with street art, parks, and restaurants. Perfect for an afternoon stroll or bike ride.

Piedmont Park

FREE

Atlanta's version of Central Park — 220 acres of green space in the heart of Midtown. Ideal for a relaxed afternoon with skyline views, a lake, walking and cycling paths, and open lawns. The park connects directly to the BeltLine Eastside Trail, making it easy to combine both in one outing.

Day 4 Sunday, Aug 2, 2026 — Wildlife & Neighborhoods

Zoo Atlanta

~$30/person

Home to one of the largest giant panda populations in the US, plus western lowland gorillas, Sumatran orangutans, African elephants, and hundreds more species. Located in Grant Park near downtown Atlanta. Plan a morning visit to beat the summer heat — allow 3–4 hours. Teens enjoy the reptile and primate exhibits.

Little Five Points

FREE

Atlanta's most eclectic and colorful neighborhood, packed with vintage shops, indie boutiques, street murals, and quirky restaurants. A fun afternoon spot for teenagers who enjoy unique street culture and local food. Grab lunch at one of the many casual eateries, then browse the vintage clothing and record stores.

High Museum of Art

~$20/person

The Southeast's leading art museum, located in Midtown Atlanta. Features an outstanding permanent collection spanning folk art, photography, decorative arts, and European masters, plus rotating international exhibitions. The striking Richard Meier–designed building is itself worth seeing. A relaxed final afternoon before the long drive to Houston tomorrow.

Dallas, TX

Aug 9 – 13, 2026  ·  4 nights

History, science, and a Fort Worth day trip

Holiday Inn Express & Suites Dallas - Plano North by IHG
3340 Central Expressway, Plano, TX 75074
Check-in Aug 9 — Check-out Aug 13 (4 nights)
Plano north suburb (~30-45 min drive to downtown Dallas via US-75). Convenient highway access to city sights, museums, and DFW area — happy to drive into the centers!
🍖

Texas Monthly Top 50 BBQ (2025) — on the drive up from Austin (Aug 9)

Your I-35 N drive passes two Top 50 joints, both an easy lunch stop: Miller's Smokehouse in Belton (~1 hr N of Austin) and Helberg Barbecue in Woodway/Waco (~midway). Check open days/hours — they sell out by early afternoon.

Day 1 Monday, Aug 10, 2026 — History & Skyline

Sixth Floor Museum

~$18/person

Located in the former Texas School Book Depository at Dealey Plaza, this museum chronicles the life, death, and legacy of President John F. Kennedy. The sixth-floor window from which Lee Harvey Oswald fired is preserved behind glass. One of America's most visited historic sites — powerful and thought-provoking for teenagers.

Reunion Tower

~$20/person

Dallas's iconic 560-ft observation ball offers 360° panoramic views of the city from the GeO-Deck. Great for photos and orientation on your first day. The nearby Klyde Warren Park — a green deck built over a freeway — is perfect for a post-visit walk and food truck lunch in the heart of the Arts District.

Deep Ellum

FREE

Dallas's most vibrant entertainment and arts district, packed with massive street murals, live music venues, craft breweries, and eclectic restaurants. Best experienced in the late afternoon and evening. A great dinner spot with something for everyone — teens will love the street art and energetic atmosphere.

Lunch Pecan Lodge — Deep Ellum

Pecan Lodge

Legendary ★★★★★
Texas BBQ • 2702 Main St, Deep Ellum, Dallas TX • $$ • Walking distance from Deep Ellum

The most celebrated BBQ inside Dallas city limits — James Beard-nominated pitmaster Justin Fourton's brisket is exceptional: rich bark, perfect smoke ring, and melt-in-your-mouth tenderness. The "Hot Mess" (brisket on a salt-crusted sweet potato with chipotle cream) is a signature must-order. Opens at 11 AM; beef ribs sell out by early afternoon — arrive at opening. Perfect lunch stop while exploring Deep Ellum.

Tip: Arrive right at 11 AM on a weekday for the shortest wait. Order brisket (fatty cut), beef rib if available, and the Hot Mess. Cash and cards accepted. Sells out daily — no exceptions.

Day 2 Tuesday, Aug 11, 2026 — Science & Nature

Perot Museum of Nature & Science

~$25/person

A stunning 180,000 sq ft science museum in downtown Dallas with 11 permanent halls covering dinosaurs, space, energy, human body, and Texas geology. The building itself — a massive cube hovering over a glass base — is an architectural showpiece. Highly interactive and engaging for teens. Allow 3–4 hours.

Dallas Arboretum

~$15/person

A spectacular 66-acre botanical garden on the shores of White Rock Lake. In summer, the gardens burst with color from thousands of seasonal blooms. Features stunning Lake views, the Children's Adventure Garden, and shaded walking paths. A beautiful and relaxing afternoon escape from the city — visit early to beat the Texas heat.

Dallas Arts District

FREE – paid shows

The largest contiguous urban arts district in the US, home to the Dallas Museum of Art (free admission), the Nasher Sculpture Center, and the stunning AT&T Performing Arts Center. Stroll along Flora Street in the evening and catch outdoor performances. The Winspear Opera House and Wyly Theatre are architectural gems worth seeing.

Shopping Evening — The Shops at Legacy West

The Shops at Legacy West

~5 min from hotel
Upscale Outdoor Mall • Legacy West, Plano TX • Free entry • Open late

The closest shopping to the hotel — a walkable open-air district in Plano with upscale and everyday brands. Lululemon, Nike, Warby Parker, Pottery Barn, Restoration Hardware, Kendra Scott, Apple, and Tesla showroom. Lined with restaurants and patios for a relaxed evening out. Easy stop after a day of sightseeing — no need to drive far. Perfect for picking up clothing, gear, or gifts on a warm Texas evening.

Tip: Combine dinner and shopping — several well-rated restaurants are inside the development. Open until 9 PM most evenings. Free parking throughout.

Day 3 Wednesday, Aug 12, 2026 — Fort Worth Day Trip

Fort Worth Stockyards

FREE entry

Step back into the Old West at this National Historic District — the last remaining authentic cattle stockyard in the US. Catch the twice-daily longhorn cattle drive down Exchange Avenue (11:30am & 4pm), visit the Cowtown Coliseum for rodeo shows, browse western wear shops, and enjoy Texas BBQ and cold drinks along the boardwalk.

Lunch Street's Fine Chicken — Chicken Fried Steak

Street's Fine Chicken

4.4 ★
Southern American • Dallas TX • $$ • ~10 min drive

Dallas's go-to for Chicken Fried Steak — the quintessential Texas comfort food. A tenderized beef cutlet deep-fried in a seasoned buttermilk crust, smothered in jalapeño cream gravy. Thick, crispy, and indulgent. Street's version is consistently ranked the best in Dallas. Also excellent for fried chicken if anyone in the family prefers it. Casual, relaxed, and family-friendly.

Tip: Go for the Chicken Fried Steak with jalapeño cream gravy — it's what Dallas is known for. Generous portions; one order is very filling. Great intro to classic Texas comfort food for the kids.

Sundance Square

FREE

Fort Worth's beautifully restored 35-block downtown entertainment district, with great restaurants, shops, street performers, and a lively plaza with a giant canopy. Very walkable and family-friendly. A great afternoon and dinner spot after the Stockyards. Fort Worth feels distinct from Dallas — more relaxed, with genuine Western character.

Kimbell Art Museum

FREE

One of America's finest small art museums, housed in Louis Kahn's masterpiece of natural-lit vaulted galleries. Free admission to the permanent collection, which includes works by Caravaggio, Velázquez, Matisse, and Picasso. Located in the Fort Worth Cultural District near the Amon Carter Museum. A world-class museum in a compact, beautiful setting.

Shopping Allen Premium Outlets

Allen Premium Outlets

~15 min from hotel
Premium Outlets • Allen, TX • 100+ stores • 25–65% off retail

The best outlet shopping in the Dallas area — 100+ brand-name stores with 25–65% off regular retail prices. Coach, Kate Spade, Michael Kors, Nike, Gap, J.Crew, Pottery Barn Outlet, Williams Sonoma Outlet, and more. Open-air layout, easy to navigate, and only 15 minutes north of the hotel in Allen, TX. The last major shopping opportunity before heading home — ideal for stocking up on clothing, shoes, and gifts at genuine outlet prices.

Tip: Allow 2–3 hours minimum. Weekday mornings are least crowded. Aug 12 is a Wednesday — one of the best days to visit. Keep all receipts for Canadian customs declaration.

Austin, TX

Aug 7 – 9, 2026  ·  2 nights

Texas capital, outdoor swimming, and live music

Hyatt Place Austin The Domain Area
3612 Tudor Boulevard, Austin, TX 78759
Check-in Aug 7 — Check-out Aug 9 (2 nights)
The Domain is a lively north Austin area (~25 min drive to Texas State Capitol/downtown via MoPac or I-35). Great restaurants/shopping on site — happy to drive into the city center!
🍖

Texas Monthly Top 50 BBQ (2025) — near The Domain

InterStellar BBQ is a statewide Top 10 pick and sits just ~10–15 min from your hotel in NW Austin — the closest Top 10 joint to any of your stays. (Austin also has Top-10 LeRoy and Lewis in South Austin, plus Franklin, La Barbecue, and Stiles Switch.) Most sell out by early afternoon — go early.

Day 1 Friday, Aug 7, 2026 — Arrival & South Austin
🍉

On your way here from Houston (Aug 7) — stop at Hempstead, TX

Take US-290 West from Houston instead of I-10 (adds ~30 min but far more scenic). Hempstead — the Watermelon Capital of Texas — sits right on US-290, ~50 miles northwest of Houston. Roadside farm stands line the highway in August, peak season, selling freshly picked melons straight from the field.

Bonus: US-290 also passes through Brenham, TX — home of Blue Bell Creameries. Free factory tours weekday mornings. Watermelon + Blue Bell ice cream on the same drive = peak Texas experience.

🍖 BBQ bonus: Brenham is also home to LJ's BBQ, a Texas Monthly Top 50 (2025) joint right on your US-290 route — a perfect lunch stop. Check its open days/hours; it sells out.

US-290 West route Hempstead · Watermelon Capital of Texas Blue Bell Creameries · Brenham Peak season in August

Texas State Capitol

FREE

Taller than the US Capitol in Washington, the stunning pink granite Texas State Capitol dominates downtown Austin. Free guided tours run daily through the beautifully restored interior, rotunda, and legislative chambers. The shaded Capitol Grounds make a good early-afternoon stop right after arriving in Austin. Allow 1–2 hours.

South Congress Avenue

FREE

"SoCo" is Austin's most iconic street — a mile of vintage shops, local boutiques, food trailers, murals, and classic Austin eateries. Home to the famous "I Love You So Much" mural and the iconic Hotel San José. Great for an early-afternoon browse and lunch. Teens love the eclectic mix of shops and the lively street atmosphere.

Barton Springs Pool

~$5/person

A beloved Austin tradition — a natural spring-fed swimming pool in Zilker Park that stays a refreshing 68°F (20°C) year-round, perfect relief from the July heat. The 300-metre pool is surrounded by grassy lawns ideal for picnics. An essential Austin experience that locals have enjoyed for generations. Perfect afternoon cool-down.

Lunch Terry Black's Barbecue

Terry Black's Barbecue

Iconic ★★★★
Texas BBQ • 1003 Barton Springs Rd, Austin TX • $$ • ~10 min from Lady Bird Lake

One of Austin's most celebrated BBQ joints — Central Texas-style smoked brisket, ribs, and sausage. All meats are smoked over post oak wood in-house. Order by the pound at the counter, grab a tray, and find a picnic table. No reservations — first come, first served. Opens at 11 AM — an easy walk-in lunch right after arriving from Houston, and steps from Barton Springs. Perfect midday stop on the Barton Springs / Lady Bird Lake side of town.

Tip: Cash-friendly but cards accepted. Get the brisket and at least one link sausage. Sells out of popular cuts by early afternoon on weekends — arrive early.

Day 2 Saturday, Aug 8, 2026 — Waterfront & Live Music

Lady Bird Lake

FREE

A stunning reservoir in the heart of Austin, ringed by a 10-mile hike-and-bike trail with skyline views. Rent kayaks, canoes, or stand-up paddleboards from the Rowing Dock or Zilker Park. The trail passes through Barton Creek Greenbelt and connects to Zilker Park — one of the best free morning activities in Austin.

Bullock Texas State History Museum

~$13/person

Texas's official state history museum, telling the epic story of the Lone Star State from prehistoric times through the Space Age. Three floors of immersive exhibits cover Native cultures, Spanish colonization, the Republic of Texas, and modern Texas. Features a giant IMAX theatre and the Texas Spirit Theater. Very engaging for teenagers.

6th Street & Live Music

FREE entry most venues

Austin bills itself as the "Live Music Capital of the World" — and 6th Street is the heart of it. Over 90 live music venues line the famous strip, with free entry to most shows on Saturday evenings. Walk the pedestrianized section, catch blues, country, or rock, and grab authentic Texas BBQ or tacos. A perfect final evening in Austin before the morning drive to Dallas.

Lunch Franklin Barbecue

Franklin Barbecue

Legendary ★★★★★
Texas BBQ • 900 E 11th St, Austin TX • $$ • ~15 min from Lady Bird Lake

Widely regarded as the best BBQ in the United States — James Beard Award winner and a bucket-list food destination. Franklin's brisket is the gold standard: impossibly tender with a perfect smoke ring and bark. Opens at 11 AM and sells out daily, often within 2–3 hours. Plan to arrive by 8–9 AM and bring chairs — the line is part of the experience. With a full free day in Austin, this is the morning to do it.

Tip: Arrive by 8–9 AM to secure a spot. Bring sunscreen, snacks, and something to sit on. Cash and cards both accepted. Once inside, order brisket (fatty cut), ribs, and turkey. They sell out — no exceptions.

Houston, TX

Aug 3 – 7, 2026  ·  4 nights

Space exploration, natural science, and city parks

Tru by Hilton Webster Houston NASA
901 Rogers Court, Webster, TX 77598
Check-in Aug 3 — Check-out Aug 7 (4 nights)
~30-45 min drive to downtown Houston via I-45. Hotel is near NASA Johnson Space Center — convenient base, happy to drive into the city core for sights!
🍖

Texas Monthly Top 50 BBQ (2025) — in Houston

Truth Barbeque (Washington Ave) is a statewide Top 10 pick — about 35–45 min from the Webster hotel. A great lunch target on any Houston day. Texas craft BBQ sells out early and often runs limited days — check hours and go early.

Day 1 Tuesday, Aug 4, 2026 — Space Center Houston

Space Center Houston

~$35/person

The official visitor center of NASA's Johnson Space Center — the hub of US human spaceflight since 1961. See actual Apollo mission spacecraft, moon rocks, a real Saturn V rocket (the largest ever built), and the historic Mission Control room from the Apollo era. The NASA tram tour takes you inside the active Johnson Space Center campus. A full-day experience — the teens will love it.

Rocket Park & Saturn V

included with admission

Within Space Center Houston, the Saturn V Center houses one of only three complete Saturn V rockets in the world — 363 feet long and awe-inspiring up close. The scale is impossible to grasp from photos. Stand beneath the five F-1 engines and understand what it took to send humans to the Moon. One of the most impressive exhibits in the United States.

NASA Mission Control

included with tram tour

The historic Apollo Mission Control room, restored to its 1969 appearance — exactly as it looked when Neil Armstrong landed on the Moon. Accessible via the NASA tram tour as part of Space Center admission. Sitting in the original flight controller seats and seeing the actual consoles used during Apollo 13 is a genuine "goosebumps" moment.

Day 2 Wednesday, Aug 5, 2026 — Museum District & Parks

Houston Museum of Natural Science

~$25/person

One of the most visited museums in the US, featuring world-class exhibits on dinosaurs (including a Quetzalcoatlus wingspan of 40 ft), gems and minerals, ancient Egypt, Texas wildlife, and an outstanding planetarium. Located in Hermann Park alongside several other free museums. Highly recommended for science-curious teens — allow 3 hours.

Hermann Park

FREE

Houston's most beloved urban park — 445 acres of gardens, a peaceful Japanese garden, a reflection pool, paddle boats on McGovern Lake, and a miniature railway. Home to the famous statue of Sam Houston, Houston's founder. The park connects the Museum of Natural Science, Houston Zoo, and Miller Outdoor Theatre. Perfect for a relaxed afternoon in the city.

Houston Zoo

~$25/person

One of the most visited zoos in the US with over 6,000 animals across 900+ species. Highlights include the African Forest with gorillas and chimps, the Natural Encounters building, and large cats. Located directly inside Hermann Park, making it easy to combine with a park visit and the Museum of Natural Science for a full final day in Houston.

Dinner Evening — The Original Ninfa's on Navigation

The Original Ninfa's on Navigation

Iconic ★★★★
Tex-Mex • 2704 Navigation Blvd, Houston • $$–$$$ • ~35 min from hotel

The birthplace of fajitas. Mama Ninfa invented the original taco al carbón here in 1973 — grilled beef sliced and served in handmade flour tortillas — launching the national fajita craze. This is the original Navigation Blvd location, open since 1973. Must-order: Mama Ninfa's Famous Taco al Carbon (the original fajita). Book a reservation ahead — call (713) 228-1175 or reserve via OpenTable. Open until 10 PM on Wednesdays.

Tip: ~35 min drive from Webster. Book ahead for a party of 4+. This is a must-do Houston dining experience — not just a restaurant, it's history.

Day 3 Thursday, Aug 6, 2026 — Galleries & Exploration

Houston Museum of Fine Arts

~$20/person

One of the largest art museums in the US, with a permanent collection of over 70,000 works spanning 6,000 years — from ancient Mediterranean art to modern masters like Picasso, Monet, and Rothko. Two main buildings connected by an underground tunnel. The Cullen Sculpture Garden outside is free and beautifully landscaped. A great half-day museum experience.

The Galleria & Houston Shopping

FREE to browse

The Galleria is Houston's largest shopping mall and one of the top ten in the US — featuring an indoor ice skating rink, 400+ stores, and dozens of restaurants. A great afternoon option to browse shops, grab lunch, and let the teens explore. Located in the Uptown district, it's also close to several upscale restaurants for a last Houston dinner.

Final Dinner in Houston

Last night in Texas

Celebrate your last evening in Texas with a proper Houston dinner. Options range from Houston's famous Tex-Mex (try Ninfa's on Navigation, the birthplace of fajitas), Gulf seafood, or a classic steakhouse. The Montrose or Midtown neighbourhoods offer a vibrant dining scene. Early bed recommended — the long return drive begins tomorrow morning.

Dining Top 5 Rated Restaurants Near the Hotel (August 13 arrival dinner)

All within ~7 mi of Comfort Inn & Suites Bellevue. After the long drive from Dallas, these options range from a 5-minute drive (HoneyFire) to Nashville's most iconic dinner spot (Loveless Cafe, 4 mi on Hwy 100).

The Loveless Cafe

4.7 ★
Southern American • ~4 mi on Hwy 100 • $$ • Open until 9 PM

A Nashville landmark since 1951 — the bucket-list Southern dinner. World-famous buttermilk biscuits served with house-made preserves (peach, strawberry, blackberry), fried chicken, and country ham. Gingham tablecloths, country music photos on the walls. Half a million guests a year. A must-do Nashville experience only 4 miles from the hotel.

Roze Pony

4.6 ★
New American • ~7 mi, Belle Meade • $$–$$$

Upscale all-day cafe and full-service restaurant in the Belle Meade neighbourhood. Creative New American menu with seasonal ingredients, craft cocktails, and a warm, relaxed atmosphere. One of Nashville's most praised neighbourhood restaurants. Reservations recommended for dinner.

Voodoo Gumbo

4.6 ★
Cajun & Creole • ~2.3 mi • $$–$$$

A unique find in Nashville — authentic Cajun and Creole cooking close to the hotel. Rich, flavourful gumbo, jambalaya, and po' boys. Casual and welcoming atmosphere. A great option if the family wants something different after days of BBQ and Tex-Mex. Walk-in friendly most evenings.

HoneyFire BBQ

4.5 ★
Nashville BBQ • ~1.5 mi, Sawyer Brown Rd • $$

The closest top-rated option — just 1.5 miles from the hotel. Ranked among the best BBQ in all of Tennessee. Counter-service, casual, and family-friendly. Sweet-profile smoked meats with outstanding brisket and ribs. Perfect low-effort option after a long drive when everyone just wants great food fast.

Fortuna Italian Steakhouse

4.3 ★
Italian & Steakhouse • ~3 mi on Hwy 100 • $$$

Cosy neighbourhood Italian steakhouse right on Hwy 100. Known for exceptional filet mignon, fresh pasta, and a welcoming atmosphere. Praised for the best bruschetta and Brussels sprouts in Nashville. A relaxed upscale option — great for a sit-down family dinner without driving far into the city.

Tip: HoneyFire BBQ is the easiest choice after a long drive — no wait, no fuss. For a true Nashville experience, Loveless Cafe is only 4 miles away and open until 9 PM. Call ahead for Roze Pony.

Full Day-by-Day Itinerary

July 25 (Sat) – Depart Brossard → Washington DC

Early departure from Brossard. Long driving day (~11 hrs total with Supercharger stops and border crossing). Arrive Washington DC by evening.

July 26 (Sun) – Washington DC: National Mall

Lincoln Memorial, Reflecting Pool, Washington Monument.

July 27 (Mon) – Washington DC: Museums & Capitol

National Air and Space Museum, U.S. Capitol Visitor Center.

July 28 (Tue) – Washington DC: White House & Virginia

White House Visitor Center, George Washington Masonic National Memorial, National Museum of the United States Army.

July 29 (Wed) – Drive to Atlanta

Drive from Washington DC to Atlanta (~10 hrs, ~1,020 km). Supercharger stops en route. Arrive Atlanta by evening, check in to hotel.

July 30 (Thu) – Atlanta: Attractions & Downtown

Georgia Aquarium, World of Coca-Cola, Centennial Olympic Park.

July 31 (Fri) – Atlanta: Buford Highway & Chinese Community

Atlanta Chinatown Mall (Chamblee), Buford Highway Farmers Market, and authentic Chinese dining along the corridor. Cash for the Chinatown Mall.

Aug 1 (Sat) – Atlanta: Day 3

Stone Mountain Park, Ponce City Market, or explore Atlanta BeltLine.

Aug 2 (Sun) – Atlanta: Day 4

Zoo Atlanta, Little Five Points neighborhood, or relax before tomorrow's drive.

Aug 3 (Mon) – Drive to Houston, TX

Drive from Atlanta to Houston (~12.5 hrs, ~1,320 km). Early departure recommended. Route: I-20 W → I-49 S → I-10 W through Alabama, Mississippi, and Louisiana. Supercharger stops: Birmingham AL, Jackson MS, Baton Rouge LA. Arrive Houston by evening.

Aug 4 (Tue) – Houston: Day 1

Space Center Houston (NASA Johnson Space Center), NASA tram tour, and astronaut exhibits — a must for the teens.

Aug 5 (Wed) – Houston: Day 2

Houston Museum of Natural Science, Hermann Park, or Houston Zoo.

Aug 6 (Thu) – Houston: Day 3

Houston Museum of Fine Arts, The Galleria, or explore Montrose/Midtown. Last night dinner in Houston.

Aug 7 (Fri) – Drive to Austin, TX + Arrival Afternoon

Leave Houston in the morning and take US-290 West through Hempstead (Watermelon Capital of Texas) and Brenham (Blue Bell Creameries) — a scenic route with roadside farm stands. Arrive Austin around noon. Afternoon: Texas State Capitol, South Congress Ave (SoCo), and Barton Springs Pool, with a walk-in lunch at Terry Black's Barbecue.

Aug 8 (Sat) – Austin: Full Day

Franklin Barbecue (arrive 8–9 AM — it sells out), Lady Bird Lake, the Bullock Texas State History Museum, and 6th Street live music in the evening — your last night in Austin.

Aug 9 (Sun) – Drive to Dallas, TX

Morning drive to Dallas (~3 hrs, ~305 km via I-35 N). Check in to Holiday Inn Express Plano by early afternoon — Dallas sightseeing begins tomorrow (Aug 10).

Aug 10 (Mon) – Dallas: Day 1

Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza (JFK assassination site), Reunion Tower observation deck, Deep Ellum for dinner.

Aug 11 (Tue) – Dallas: Day 2

Perot Museum of Nature and Science, Dallas Arboretum, Dallas Arts District.

Aug 12 (Wed) – Dallas: Day 3

Fort Worth day trip (~45 min): Fort Worth Stockyards, Sundance Square, or Kimbell Art Museum.

Aug 13 (Thu) – Drive: Dallas, TX → Nashville, TN (~1,050 km / ~10.5 hrs)

Early departure from Plano hotel. Route: I-30 E through Texarkana and Little Rock, AR, then I-40 E into Nashville. Supercharger stops: Texarkana TX, Little Rock AR, Memphis TN (optional). Overnight at Comfort Inn & Suites Nashville Bellevue.

Aug 14 (Fri) – Drive: Nashville, TN → Cleveland, OH (~870 km / ~8.5 hrs)

Route: I-65 N through Louisville, KY, I-71 N through Cincinnati and Cleveland, OH. Supercharger stops: Elizabethtown KY / Louisville, Cincinnati OH, Cleveland area. Overnight at Hampton Inn & Suites Cleveland Beachwood.

Aug 15 (Sat) – Drive: Cleveland, OH → Brossard, QC (~900 km / ~9.5 hrs) 🏠

Final day home. Route via I-90 / northern highways to border at Champlain/Lacolle (allow 20–40 min), then A-15 N. Supercharger stops as needed en route. Arrive home mid-afternoon!

Atlanta Shopping July 29 – Aug 3 · 5 nights · Tax ~8.9%

5 nights gives the most shopping flexibility of the trip. Buckhead has the best luxury malls; the outlet options are within 45 min drive. Best days: any weekday morning (least crowded).

Lenox Square

Luxury

Atlanta's premier luxury mall in Buckhead. 250+ stores including Fendi, Burberry, Cartier, Bloomingdale's, Macy's, and Apple. Anchor for upscale fashion and jewellery. Great food court and restaurants. ~25 min from hotel.

Fendi · Burberry · Cartier Apple Store ~25 min from hotel

Ultra-luxury

The Southeast's premier luxury destination — directly across from Lenox Square. Gucci, Prada, Tom Ford, Tiffany & Co., Saks Fifth Avenue. Also has a Legoland Discovery Centre for the kids. Can pair both malls in one day.

Local & Unique

Top 5 US

Ranked one of the top 5 shopping centres in the entire United States. 230+ stores across 2 million sq ft. Neiman Marcus, Nordstrom, Macy's plus luxury boutiques and mainstream favourites. Museum-quality art installations throughout. A destination in itself — allow 3–4 hours.

Neiman Marcus · Nordstrom 230+ stores ~25 min from hotel
🏬

Allen Premium Outlets

Best outlets

The best outlet mall in the Dallas area — 100+ brands with 25–65% off retail. Located in Allen, just north of Plano and very close to the hotel. Coach, Kate Spade, Michael Kors, Nike, Gap, Pottery Barn, Williams Sonoma Outlet, and more. The top choice for value shopping in the Dallas leg.

25–65% off retail Coach · Kate Spade · Nike ~15 min from hotel
⛸️

Galleria Dallas

Family-friendly

200+ stores over 4 floors with a full-size indoor ice rink at the centre. Great mix of mainstream and premium brands. Kids can skate while parents shop. Dining options on every level. An easy, all-weather family shopping day with built-in entertainment.

200+ stores Indoor ice rink ~30 min from hotel
🛒

Knox-Henderson District

Local & Unique

Dallas's most interesting neighbourhood shopping strip — local boutiques, vintage shops, home décor, and gastro-pubs. Knox side has home décor and traditional shops; Henderson side has independent clothing boutiques and patio restaurants. Good for unique gifts and non-mall shopping. Near downtown Dallas.

Vintage & boutiques Home décor Near downtown
🎨

Deep Ellum

Art & Souvenirs

Already on the Day 1 itinerary — while you're there for the murals and Pecan Lodge, check out the independent art galleries, record shops, and creative boutiques. Great for Dallas-specific souvenirs, local art prints, and gifts. The most characterful shopping in Dallas.

Local art & galleries Record shops Already on Day 1

🇨🇦 Canadian Customs — Personal Exemption

After 21 days outside Canada, each family member qualifies for the full $800 CAD duty-free personal exemption.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Family of 4
Up to $3,200 CAD total duty-free across the family — coordinate purchases to spread across all 4 people.
📦 What counts
Goods for personal use, gifts, and souvenirs. Keep your US receipts — CBSA may ask for them at the border.
🏁 Best crossing
Champlain/Lacolle (I-87 → A-15) or Niagara. Both are well-staffed and familiar with cross-border shoppers.
Smart shopping strategy: Atlanta (5 nights) is your best opportunity — use Day 2 on Buford Hwy for Asian goods, then save a weekday for Lenox Square/Phipps or North Georgia Premium Outlets. In Dallas, hit Allen Premium Outlets (15 min from hotel) first for value, then Legacy West for the experience. Buy bulk/heavy items in Dallas rather than Atlanta to reduce carrying time. Keep all US receipts for CBSA — you have 21+ days outside Canada so the full $800 CAD/person exemption applies.
